message.content:
Add a real binding between the admin board's `App` entity and the platform's `Server` entity in the Nxeon app (/opt/nxeon, Next.js + Prisma, dark theme), plus two small data cleanups, then commit/push and deploy to STAGING ONLY (do NOT promote to production). The working tree is clean at commit 5e28208. Read the relevant files before editing.

BACKGROUND: The board `App` model (prisma/schema.prisma, ~line 915) is currently `{id, name, slug @unique, color, createdAt, boards Board[]}` — a standalone label with NO link to real infrastructure. The platform has a `Server` model (with fields including id, name, ipAddress, status). We want each board App to optionally point at a real Server so the board is app-aware.

=== CHANGE 1: Schema — App ↔ Server binding ===
- Add to `App`: `serverId String?` and `server Server? @relation(fields: [serverId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)`.
- Add the back-relation on `Server`: `boardApps App[]` (pick a name that doesn't collide with existing relations on Server — verify).
- Apply with `npx prisma db push` (this DB uses push). Confirm it applies cleanly to the production `nxeon` DB (additive/nullable, safe).

=== CHANGE 2: Data — bind the existing apps + cleanups (write a tsx script under scripts/, run with npx tsx, then delete it; async main() wrapper — top-level await unsupported) ===
- Look up servers by IP: bind the app with slug `soul-pilates` → the Server whose `ipAddress === "51.79.226.200"`; bind the app with slug `studionexis` (display name "Studio Nexis") → the Server whose `ipAddress === "51.79.226.215"`. Leave the `nxeon` app's serverId null (it represents the platform itself, which has no customer Server row). Print which server name each resolved to; if an IP matches no server, report it and skip that binding (don't guess).
- Ensure the `studionexis`-slug app's `name` is `"Studio Nexis"` (it should already be; leave color as-is).
- DELETE the app with slug `test` (it has 0 boards) — `db.app.delete`. If it has boards for any reason, reassign them to null first, then delete.

=== CHANGE 3: seed.ts durability (prisma/seed.ts, ~line 47-50) ===
- The apps array seeds `{ slug: "studionexis", name: "studionexis", color: "#38bdf8" }` and upserts with `update: { name, color }`, which would REVERT the "Studio Nexis" rename on any re-seed. Change that entry's `name` to `"Studio Nexis"`. Do NOT add a `test` app to the seed. Do NOT seed serverId (server ids are environment-specific) — leave binding to the data script / picker.

=== CHANGE 4: UI — server picker + show bound server (components/admin/BoardClient.tsx, app/admin/board/page.tsx, lib/actions-board.ts) ===
- Add a server picker so an App can be bound to / unbound from a Server. Reuse an existing server-list source if one exists (grep lib/ for a `listServers`/server-fetching server action; if none is easily reusable, add a small admin-gated `listServersForBinding()` in lib/actions-board.ts returning `{id,name,ipAddress,status}[]`). Add a server action `setAppServer(appId, serverId|null)` (admin-gated, revalidatePath("/admin/board")).
- Surface it in the App management UI: when creating an app or via a small edit affordance on the app pill (e.g. a tiny gear/menu, or in the "+App"/app context), let the admin choose the bound server. Show the bound server's name (and a small status dot if available) somewhere unobtrusive on the selected app's header — so it's clear which real server the app maps to. Keep it cohesive with the dark theme; don't clutter the header you just decluttered.
- Make `listBoards`/`getBoard`/the page include the app's `server` relation so the UI can display it. Preserve all existing board behavior.
- Do NOT try to wire the Epic-C stage-action buttons to the bound server in this task — that's a separate follow-up (each app has its own deploy mechanism). Just the binding + display + picker.

=== AFTER EDITS ===
1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — zero errors in touched files.
2. `npm run build` — must compile.
3. `git add` ONLY the files you changed (schema.prisma, seed.ts, BoardClient.tsx, page.tsx, lib/actions-board.ts). NEVER `git add -A`; never stage `scripts/_*.ts` or secrets. Commit (message ending `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>`); the post-commit hook auto-pushes to origin main — confirm via `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main`.
4. Deploy to STAGING ONLY: `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh`; verify exit 0 + HTTP 200 on port 8080.
5. **DO NOT run scripts/promote-production.sh.** Stop after staging.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT touch the Soul Pilates .200 box services, DNS, or mail config (you may READ the Server rows' IPs from the nxeon DB via Prisma — that's fine).
- Do NOT `git add -A`.
- If a safety classifier blocks a command, report it verbatim and stop.

Return a structured report: schema change, which server each app resolved+bound to (by name/IP), test-app deletion result, seed.ts change, the picker UI added, typecheck/build status, commit hash + push confirmation, staging health, and explicit confirmation you did NOT deploy to production.

385	  ///
386	  /// WHY A PERCENT AND NOT A CENTS RATE. Proration is a DIFFERENCE between two
387	  /// plans' rates. A stored $/mo figure prices only the plan the server is on and
388	  /// says nothing about the plan it is moving to, so the other half of the
389	  /// subtraction would still need a basis invented for it — which is the bug. A
390	  /// percent is a rate BASIS that applies to any plan price, so both halves of the
391	  /// delta come from this one persisted number and the round trip is symmetric by
392	  /// construction rather than by convention. It also survives a plan change with no
393	  /// write at all: the customer keeps the rate they bought at, so up-then-down is
394	  /// exactly zero.
395	  ///
396	  ///   0   = full price. What BOTH renewal paths bill (worker/billing.ts sweep and
397	  ///         lib/actions.ts renewNow charge `vpsTermPriceCents` with no promo), and
398	  ///         what a flat-priced game plan is sold at.
399	  ///   1-99= a genuine intro/seasonal discount, or a blend of paid and gifted
400	  ///         months (see prorateBlendPercent in lib/proration.ts).
401	  ///   100 = gifted. Nothing was paid for these months, so nothing may prorate out
402	  ///         of them — an admin extension/free grant records this.
403	  ///   NULL= unknown. Only on rows that predate this column; resolved by an
404	  ///         EXPLICIT conservative fallback (`resolveTermPromoPercent`), never by
405	  ///         falling through to today's promo, because that IS the bug above.
406	  ///
407	  /// FLOAT, not Int, even though every promo in the catalogue is a whole number.
408	  /// Blending a renewal into a part-used term lands on halves: 36 months at 45% off
409	  /// plus 36 renewed at full price is exactly 22.5% off, and rounding that to 23
410	  /// quietly shaves $7.20 off a $1,071.36 credit. A first term still stores the
411	  /// promo's exact integer, so the column reads the same for the common case.
412	  termPromoPercent    Float?
413	  /// GB of root disk purchased BEYOND the plan's `diskGB`. The server's EFFECTIVE
414	  /// disk is always `plan.diskGB + extraDiskGB`, so the extra survives a plan
415	  /// resize (it is additive to whichever plan the server sits on). Growth is
416	  /// ONE-WAY: shrinking a live filesystem risks data loss, so nothing anywhere
